# Prisoner Handling
## Arrest and Processing Procedure
1. Prisoners [color=#ff0000]must[/color] be read their list of crimes before sentencing can commence. Sentencing should be done in accordance with Corporate Law. Any time spent in processing and confinement [color=#ff0000]must[/color] be subtracted from the total time of their sentence.
2. Arrested prisoners are to be searched upon entry to Security. IDs, PDAs, and searched items are to be [color=#ff0000]removed[/color] from prisoners while in confinement. Prisoners are to be provided/allowed their own radio communications equipment.
Prisoner searches include: - Pockets - PDA Slot - Bags - Coats/overwear
3. Once an arrest has been made, the prisoner should be marked as "[color=#2a6099]Detained[/color]" in the Security Records Computer, and an Arrest Report should be filled out at the earliest convenience. Arrest reports may be waived in the face of [color=#8d281e]imminent station destruction[/color], or if hostilities are still ongoing. There can be time for paperwork later.
4. Once a prisoner has served their sentence, their possessions should be returned to them and they should be marked as "[color=#2a6099]Discharged[/color]" in the Security Records Computer. Prisoners' temporary IDs should be recovered and stored in a secure location following their release.
## Prisoner Treatment
1. Prisoners placed into confinement are to be unrestrained. Prisoners who become combative or pose a flight risk may be restrained at the Warden's discretion.
2. Prisoners not accused of a violent crime are permitted to keep their current clothing unless there is evidence beyond reasonable doubt that said clothing is contraband or may aid in their escape.
3. Prisoners are to be kept watch of where possible, and should be provided adequate sustenance and enrichment. Prisoners who attempt to escape should be prevented using [color=#ffe100]non-lethal means[/color].
## Legal Rights
1. If there is an [color=#ffe100]Internal Affairs Agent[/color] or [color=#ffe100]Magistrate[/color] on shift, prisoners may request a review of their sentencing if they believe it to be wrongful or draconic.
2. Prisoners who receive permanent or execution sentences may [color=#00a933]request a trial[/color] for their crimes, as decided by a jury of 12 of their peers. This may be waived in the face of [color=#8d281e]imminent station destruction[/color].
3. Prisoners may request a copy of their arrest report following their release.
